subject: enemy_intent_evidence_gap
claim: For client revision r806919.Wizard_1_610, the repository does not yet contain a verified own-client observation showing whether enemy intent is announced before a combat round resolves, which message carries it, or when it becomes visible.
how_to_repeat: Read README.md's current-status table and confirm that combat is not yet available in Ambrose.
Read doc/roadmap/phase-11-real-combat.md and treat its creature AI, turn, and combat-message sections as planned implementation work rather than observed behavior.
Search contrib/findings/combat/ and the repository history for an own-client capture that records a mob action announcement before a round resolves.

Run the missing experiment against a local combat-capable server and the user's own r806919 client: start a duel, record the visible enemy intent and all relevant messages with timestamps before and during resolution, and repeat with different creature actions without committing capture bytes.
evidence: README.md states that combat is not yet available in the current project state.
Phase 11.15 plans weighted creature AI and phase 11.01 plans turn-order execution, but their acceptance checks are future work and do not establish a retail client observation of enemy intent.
The phase-11 document lists planned combat message names and creature data sources but contains no completed timing record for an enemy-action announcement.
No file exists under contrib/findings/combat/ in this checkout, and no combat capture, client asset, or extracted client data was added to the repository.
disproof: A repository-approved own-client combat experiment for r806919 that records an enemy intent announcement, identifies its message and fields, and measures when the client receives or displays it relative to round resolution.
